title: NeuroSYNC — UK Multidisciplinary Centre for Neuromorphic Systems and Computing
summary: The Aston–Hartree Neuromorphic Centre of Competence was launched on 2025-10-21 with £5.6 million EPSRC funding to advance neuromorphic computing in the UK. NeuroSYNC submitted evidence regarding low-energy AI solutions to Parliament's Science, Innovation and Technology Committee. A new strategic partnership between Aston University and STFC Hartree Centre aims to accelerate technology translation and industrial adoption. Applications for Associated Members are open as of 2026-05-14. The International Neuromorphic Computing Conference (INCC) is scheduled for May 2027 in London.
tldr: NeuroSYNC launched a new UK neuromorphic centre with £5.6m funding and submitted parliamentary evidence on low-energy computing strategies.
evidence: The partnership establishes the Aston–Hartree Neuromorphic Centre of Competence, bringing together academia, industry and the public sector
NeuroSYNC has submitted written evidence to the UK Parliament's Science, Innovation and Technology Committee as part of its inquiry into Low-Energy Computing (Reference: LEC0016)
